{{short description|Type of graph in graph theory}}
{{About||the nomogram technique in radio frequency engineering|Smith chart|the Biggs–Smith distance-regular graph|Biggs–Smith graph}}

{{Unfocused|date=November 2024}}
In the mathematical field of [[graph theory]], a '''Smith graph''' is either of two kinds of graph.

*It is a graph whose [[adjacency matrix]] has largest eigenvalue at most 2,<ref>{{cite conference|editor=Richard Guy|title=Combinatorial Structures and Their Applications | conference=Proceedings of the Calgary International Conference on Combinatorial Structures and Their Applications |place=University of Calgary, Calgary, Alberta, Canada |date=June 2–14, 1969 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rThqxwEACAAJ |publisher=Gordon and Breach |author=John H. Smith |chapter=Some properties of the spectrum of a graph |pages=403–406}}</ref> or has spectral radius 2<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.disc.2006.11.049 |title=Decomposition of Smith graphs in maximal reflexive cacti |journal=Discrete Mathematics |volume=308 |issue=2–3 |pages=355–366 |year=2008 |last1=Radosavljević |first1=Z. |last2=Mihailović |first2=B. |last3=Rašajski |first3=M. |doi-access= }}</ref> or at most 2.<ref>{{cite journal |jstor=26359061 |title=Spectral Theory of Smith Graphs |journal=Bulletin (Académie Serbe des Sciences et des Arts. Classe des Sciences Mathématiques et Naturelles. Sciences Mathématiques) |issue=42 |pages=19–40 |last1=Cvetković |first1=Dragoš |year=2017 }}</ref>  The graphs with spectral radius 2 form two infinite families and three sporadic examples; if we ask for spectral radius at most 2 then there are two additional infinite families and three more sporadic examples. The infinite families with spectral radius less than 2 are the [[Path (graph theory)|path]]s and the [[Path (graph theory)|path]]s with one extra edge attached to the vertex next to an endpoint; the infinite families with spectral radius exactly 2 are the [[Cycle (graph theory)|cycle]]s and the [[Path (graph theory)|path]]s with an extra edge attached to each of the vertices next to an endpoint.
These are also the simply laced [[Dynkin_diagram#Affine_Dynkin_diagrams|affine (and finite, if the spectral radius may be less than 2) Dynkin diagram]]s. 
*It is a [[strongly regular graph]] with certain kinds of parameter values.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Cameron | first1 = P. J.
 | last2 = Goethals | first2 = J.-M.
 | last3 = Seidel | first3 = J. J.
 | doi = 10.1016/0021-8693(78)90220-X
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Journal of Algebra
 | mr = 523457
 | pages = 257–280
 | title = Strongly regular graphs having strongly regular subconstituents
 | volume = 55
 | year = 1978}}</ref>
